registry_schema_notes.purpose: Single source of truth for every MCP tool. The Python server reads name/title/description/input_schema/annotations/toolsets/timeout_s; the Ruby bridge reads handler_key/mutates/operation/api/title.

fields.name: MCP tool name, [a-z][a-z0-9_]*, unique. Claude Code shows it as mcp__sketchup__<name> (keep that under 64 characters).
fields.title: Human title; also the undo name 'MCP: <title>' for model-changing tools.
fields.runs_on: bridge = executed inside SketchUp by Na__CommandRouter; server = answered by the Python server alone.
fields.mutates: true = changes the model: refused in read-only mode, wrapped in one undo operation unless operation is false.
fields.operation: false = the handler manages undo itself (or must not be inside an operation, e.g. model_undo).
fields.api: SketchUp Ruby API methods the tool cannot work without. Checked offline against the official stubs index and live at bridge start; a tool with a missing dependency is refused with that reason.
fields.toolsets: core = the 22-tool set for clients with tool limits (--toolset core); every tool is in full.
fields.timeout_s: How long the Python server waits for SketchUp before reporting 'status unknown' (never auto-retried).
fields.property_since: Top level: {"tool.parameter": "x.y.z"}, the bridge version a parameter added later needs. A SketchUp window whose bridge predates it would ignore the parameter and answer as if it were not there, so the server pings the window's bridge and refuses the call with the fix (Reload Plugin Data). List every parameter added to an existing tool here. A value added later, such as a new action, is listed as "tool.parameter=value" (1.0.23): an older bridge would refuse it without naming the fix.
fields.$use: Inside input_schema, {"$use": "name"} is replaced by common_schemas[name] (plus any sibling keys, e.g. a longer description) when the Python server loads this file.

registry_schema_notes.adding_a_tool: Add an entry here, add a handler method in 10__BridgeHandlers, add its route in Na__CommandRouter, run 40__Tests__Validation, then Reload Plugin Data and restart the MCP server.

server.name: sketchup
server.title: Na SketchUp MCP
server.description: Inspect, model, paint, tag, view and capture a live SketchUp 2026 model. Built by Noble Architecture.

frame.description: Slice at any angle: min, max, view, axis, path and every position in and out are in this frame instead of the model's axes, and the reply echoes it (origin, unit axes, and the rule back to the model). Give origin (a model point, default [0, 0, 0]) and then angle (degrees anticlockwise from +x about the vertical: x along it, y level to its left, z up), or x_axis with an optional y_axis (made square to x; without it y is level, to x's left); or id alone: a group or component whose origin and axes make the frame. top looks down the frame's z, front along its +y. Needs Na Point Cloud Viewer 0.14.6.

origin.description: The frame's origin, a model point (default [0, 0, 0]).

angle.description: Degrees anticlockwise from +x about the vertical: x along it, y level to its left, z up.

x_axis.description: The frame's x (any length): along a wall, up a roof's slope.

y_axis.description: Optional: made square to x_axis (default level, to x's left).

id.description: A group or component whose origin and axes make the frame (with nothing else).

units.description: Unit for every length in this call's input AND output. Default mm. 'model' = the model's own display unit.

id.description: Persistent id of an entity (the 'id' returned by entity_query, outliner_tree, selection_get).

ids.description: Persistent ids of entities (from entity_query, outliner_tree, selection_get).

path.description: Optional instance path: ids of the groups/components from the model root down to the container. Only needed when a component is used several times and you mean one particular copy.

point.description: [x, y, z] in the call's units (z defaults to 0).

points.description: List of [x, y, z] points in the call's units.

vector.description: [x, y, z] displacement in the call's units.

direction.description: [x, y, z] direction (unitless, any length except zero).

parent_id.description: Where new geometry goes. Omit = the active context (the open group, else the model root). 0 = model root. Otherwise the id of a group/component whose definition receives it.

coords.description: Frame of the given points. world (default) = model axes, correct at any nesting depth and inside open groups. local = the parent's own axes.

name.description: Name shown in the Outliner, as the user would call it (e.g. "Wall - North"), following the naming style already in the model. Always pass one: without it the object is named from its kind and size, e.g. "Box 1200 x 600 x 150".

tag.description: Tag (layer) name, created if missing. "Untagged" for none.

material.description: Material name, "#RRGGBB" for a plain colour (created and reused on demand), or "none".

offset.description: Items to skip, for paging (use next_offset from the previous call).

response_format.description: concise (default): id, type, name, tag, material, world bounds. detailed: adds placement, size, volume, counts, attribute dictionary names.

camera.description: Camera in world coordinates. Any subset of fields.

fov.description: Field of view in degrees (perspective only).

ortho_height.description: Visible height for parallel projection, in the call's units.

standard_view.description: Point the camera at the model (or at zoom_ids) from a standard direction. front looks along +Y; iso is from front-right-above.

tools.name: sketchup_status
tools.title: SketchUp Status
tools.description: Call this first. Reports whether SketchUp is connected, its version and licence (Pro is needed for solid_boolean), the open model (title, path, unsaved changes), the active edit context (open groups), selection count, active tool and scene, the bridge's read-only / Ruby-eval settings, and any tools unavailable in this SketchUp. Lists every running SketchUp window (each is a separate process), with selected true on the one in use. The server stays on that window: one opened later never takes over. Pass select_pid to direct all later calls to another window. If the window in use closes, calls are refused until you do. If SketchUp is not connected, the reply says how to start the bridge (Extensions > Na SketchUp MCP > Bridge Running).

select_pid.description: Switch this MCP server to the SketchUp process with this pid (from 'instances').

include_extensions.description: Also list installed SketchUp extensions (name, version, loaded).

tools.name: model_info
tools.title: Model Info
tools.description: Overview of the open model: title, path, description, unsaved changes, the model's unit settings (UnitsOptions with readable names), world bounds, counts (root entities by type, total faces, component and group definitions, materials, tags, tag folders, scenes, styles), active context, active tag / scene / style, and location (georeferenced, latitude, longitude, north angle). include_statistics walks the whole hierarchy and counts every entity type including nested copies (can be slow on big models; capped and reported as truncated).

include_statistics.description: Walk the full hierarchy and count entities by type (default false).

tools.name: model_settings
tools.title: Model Settings
tools.description: Change model-wide settings: display units (Model Info > Units), the model description, and geo-location. Only keys this SketchUp really has are accepted (read them from model_info units_options); unknown keys are refused with the valid list. This changes how SketchUp DISPLAYS lengths; it does not change geometry, and it does not change the units this MCP server uses (that is each call's 'units' argument).

units_options.description: Raw UnitsOptions keys and values, e.g. {"LengthSnapEnabled": false}.

tools.name: model_file
tools.title: Model File
tools.description: File operations. action: save (to its current path), save_as (.skp path; the model now lives there), save_copy (.skp copy; the open model keeps its path), open (.skp; replaces the open model), new (empty model), export (3D/CAD/PDF by extension: dae, kmz, obj, fbx, stl, 3ds, dwg, dxf, ifc, pdf, glb, usdz, wrl, xsi - some need Pro), import (dwg, dxf, 3ds, dae, kmz, stl, ifc, images...; for .skp use component_place skp_path). Never overwrites a file unless overwrite:true and never discards unsaved work unless discard_unsaved_changes:true: only pass those when the user explicitly asked. options = the documented exporter/importer options for that format (e.g. {"units": "mm", "triangulated_faces": true}); unknown option names are rejected with the valid list. Summary dialogs are always off. For PNG/JPG images of the view use view_capture.

path.description: Absolute file path. Its extension picks the export/import format.

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file (default false).

discard_unsaved_changes.description: For open/new: throw away unsaved changes in the current model (default false). Only with the user's explicit agreement.

options.description: Exporter/importer options documented by SketchUp for this format (see ruby_api_lookup query 'exporter options').

selection_only.description: Export only the current selection (sets selectionset_only).

tools.name: sketchup_open_window
tools.title: Open in New Window
tools.description: Open a .skp in a NEW SketchUp window, so every window already open keeps its model and its unsaved work (model_file open replaces the model in the window in use). copy_to (a folder, or a .skp path) copies the file first and opens the copy, so the original is never open and can never be saved over: use it whenever you only need to read a project model or try something on it. Waits until the new window's bridge answers with that model open, then switches this server to it (select:false to stay where you are). A file already open in a running window is used as it is. Windows only; starts the SketchUp version this server belongs to.

path.description: Absolute path of the .skp to open.

copy_to.description: Open a copy instead: a folder (the copy keeps the file name) or a .skp path.

overwrite.description: With copy_to: replace an existing copy (default false).

select.description: Switch this server to the new window (default true).

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for the new window's bridge (default 240).

tools.name: sketchup_close_window
tools.title: Close Window
tools.description: Close a SketchUp window (pid from sketchup_status) the way File > Exit does, and wait until it has gone. Close the windows you opened with sketchup_open_window as soon as you have what you need: every open SketchUp holds a lot of memory. A model with unsaved changes is refused and left open; discard_unsaved_changes:true throws those changes away, so pass it only when the user has agreed. If it was the window this server used, choose another with sketchup_status select_pid.

discard_unsaved_changes.description: Close even with unsaved changes, losing them (default false). Only with the user's explicit agreement.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for it to close (default 60).

tools.name: model_purge
tools.title: Purge Unused
tools.description: Remove unused component definitions, materials, tags, styles and (SketchUp 2025+) environments, like Window > Model Info > Statistics > Purge Unused. Components are purged first so the materials and tags they held can go too. Returns how many of each were removed. One undo step.

tools.name: entity_query
tools.title: Query Entities
tools.description: Find entities and get their ids. Searches one context (default: the active context; parent_id 0 = model root; or inside a group/component), optionally recursive into nested groups, or the current selection. Filters combine (AND): types, name_contains (instance or definition name), definition_name, tag, material ('none' = default material), attribute {dictionary, key?, value?}, visibility. Paged with limit/offset; 'total' counts every match and next_offset is null on the last page. Each result has world-space bounds in the call's units; nested results carry 'path' (ids from the root). Use entity_get for full detail on a few ids.

parent_id.description: Where to look. Omit = active context. 0 = model root. Else a group/component id (searches inside it).

recursive.description: Also search inside nested groups/components (default false).

types.description: Entity types to include (Instance = Group + ComponentInstance).

name_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring of the instance or definition name.

selection_only.description: Search the current selection instead of a context.

tools.name: list_entities
tools.title: List Entities
tools.description: List and filter entities in a context (alias for entity_query). Searches the active context by default (parent_id 0 = model root; or inside a group/component), optionally recursive into nested groups, or the current selection. Filters combine (AND): types, name_contains, definition_name, tag, material ('none' = default material), attribute {dictionary, key?, value?}, visibility. Paged with limit/offset; each result has world-space bounds in the call's units.

parent_id.description: Where to look. Omit = active context. 0 = model root. Else a group/component id (searches inside it).

recursive.description: Also search inside nested groups/components (default false).

types.description: Entity types to include (Instance = Group + ComponentInstance).

name_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring of the instance or definition name.

selection_only.description: Search the current selection instead of a context.

tools.name: entity_get
tools.title: Get Entity Details
tools.description: Full detail for up to 100 ids: type, names, tag, material, world bounds, and by type - faces (world area, world normal, vertex count, holes, back material), edges (world length, soft/smooth, curve/arc centre and radius), groups/components (world placement: origin, unit axes, scale, mirrored, rotation_xyz degrees; oriented size; volume and manifold; entity count; copies of the definition; attribute dictionaries), text, dimensions, section planes, images, definitions, materials, tags. include_geometry adds world coordinates (face loops, edge ends, guide positions). Attribute values are included by default (long strings truncated).

include_geometry.description: Add world coordinates of vertices/endpoints (default false).

tools.name: outliner_tree
tools.title: Outliner Tree
tools.description: The group/component hierarchy, like SketchUp's Outliner: id, type, name, definition, tag, hidden, locked and children for every group/component, plus counts of loose geometry per level (faces, edges...). Start here to understand how a model is organised. Default root is the model root (parent_id to start inside a group). Depth and siblings are capped (max_depth, max_children); deeper levels report nested_instances_not_shown.

parent_id.description: Start inside this group/component (default 0 = model root).

include_loose_counts.description: Count loose faces/edges per level (default true).

include_bounds.description: Add world bounds per node (default false).

tools.name: collection_list
tools.title: List Collection
tools.description: List a model collection: materials (colour, alpha, texture size; detailed adds PBR), tags (visible, colour, line style, folder, active), tag_folders, scenes (flags for what each scene remembers, style; detailed adds camera and timings), definitions (component definitions with instance counts and size; groups/images excluded unless asked; detailed adds file, behaviour, attributes), styles, line_styles, environments (2025+). include_usage counts how many faces/entities use each material or tag. Filter with name_contains; paged with limit/offset.

include_usage.description: materials/tags: count elements using each (default false).

used_only.description: definitions: only those with instances (default false).

tools.name: selection_get
tools.title: Get Selection
tools.description: What the user has selected: count, count by type, the combined world bounds, and paged summaries with ids. When the user says 'this', 'these' or 'the selected ...', call this first. The selection always belongs to the active context (the open group, if any), which is also returned.

tools.name: selection_set
tools.title: Set Selection
tools.description: Change the selection to show the user what you mean or to prepare a native tool: replace (default), add, remove, toggle (need ids), clear, invert, select_all (active context). Only entities of the active context can be selected; to select inside a group, open it first with context_set. Does not change the model or the undo stack.

tools.name: context_set
tools.title: Set Edit Context
tools.description: Open a group/component for editing (like double-clicking it) or close back out. open: pass the id; its full path from the root is worked out for you (pass path to choose a particular copy of a shared component). close: one level up. close_all: back to the model root. Needed before selecting or grouping entities inside a group. Locked instances and Live Components cannot be opened. Cannot be used inside an atomic batch_execute (it splits SketchUp's undo operation).

tools.name: geometry_measure
tools.title: Measure
tools.description: Measure in world units. ids: combined world bounds, total face area (true world area even inside scaled/rotated nested groups; groups/components measure everything inside them), total edge length, face/edge counts, and solid volume (manifold groups/components only; non-solids are listed). points: segment lengths, total and straight distance of a polyline. raytest: cast a ray from origin along direction and report what it hits (point, distance, entity id, path), e.g. find the floor below a point or what a wall faces; max_hits > 1 lists everything along the ray.

measure.description: What to measure for ids (default bounds, area, volume).

tools.name: geometry_draw
tools.title: Draw Geometry
tools.description: Draw lines and planar shapes, optionally filled and extruded. kind: line (2 points), polyline (points, closed?), rectangle (2 opposite corners on a plane parallel to XY/XZ/YZ, or 3 points: corner, end of first side, point setting the second side), circle / polygon (center, radius, normal, segments/sides), arc (center, radius, x_axis = start direction, normal, start_angle, end_angle in degrees), face (points = outer loop, holes = inner loops). Closed shapes are filled unless fill_face:false; extrude pushes the face by that distance along its normal. Face normals follow the right-hand rule of the points (counter-clockwise from above = up) or 'normal', never SketchUp's ground-plane quirk, so extrude > 0 goes up for a CCW footprint. Closed shapes default to wrap_in:'group' (never merges with existing geometry); lines default to 'none' (they split faces they are drawn on). Returns the new group's id, or the new face/edge ids when unwrapped. Pass name for wrapped shapes: it is how the user finds them in the Outliner.

closed.description: polyline: join the last point to the first (and fill).

holes.description: face: inner loops to cut out.

fill_face.description: Create the face for closed shapes (default true).

extrude.description: Push/pull the new face by this distance along its normal.

wrap_in.description: Container for the new geometry (default group for closed shapes, none for lines).

definition_name.description: Definition name when wrap_in is component.

tools.name: geometry_create_solid
tools.title: Create Solid
tools.description: Create a closed solid in its own group (or component): box (size [x, y, z]), cylinder, cone, prism, pyramid (radius, height; prism/pyramid use sides), tube (radius, inner_radius, height), sphere, hemisphere (radius), torus (radius to tube centre, minor_radius). Faces point outward, curved surfaces are softened, the result is manifold (ready for solid_boolean and volume). position is where the anchor goes: corner = min corner (default for box), base_center (default for most), center (default for sphere/torus). Orientation: rotation_z (degrees about the solid's own vertical) and/or z_axis / x_axis. The group's own axes follow the solid, so later rotate/scale edits behave naturally. Works in any parent at any depth. Always pass name (what the user would call it): it is how they find it in the Outliner.

size.description: box: [width x, depth y, height z].

rotation_z.description: Degrees about the solid's vertical axis.

tools.name: geometry_create_mesh
tools.title: Create Mesh
tools.description: Build arbitrary geometry fast from a vertex list and polygons (indices into vertices, 3+ each, counter-clockwise seen from outside). Uses SketchUp's EntitiesBuilder (2022+): vertices and edges are shared, nothing merges with existing geometry. Non-planar polygons are split into triangles automatically. smooth:true softens edges between faces meeting at less than smooth_angle (default 30 degrees). soft_edges / hard_edges / smooth_edges / quad_edges set single edges by their two vertex indices [i, j], after smooth, in that order: hard_edges hard; smooth_edges drawn but shaded smooth; soft_edges soft and smooth (hidden); quad_edges are QuadFace Tools dividing edges (soft, smooth, no shadow), so two triangles read as one quad. The result counts them. Up to 50,000 polygons per call; wrapped in a new group by default. Always pass name: it is how the user finds it in the Outliner. Faces are made consistent and closed shells are turned outward, so a closed mesh is a real solid whatever the winding; the result reports open shells.

soft_edges.description: Edges to soften and smooth, each [i, j]: two vertex indices of an edge of the polygons. Applied after smooth.

hard_edges.description: Edges to keep hard (not soft, not smooth), each [i, j]. Applied after smooth, before soft_edges.

smooth_edges.description: Edges drawn but shaded smooth (soft off, smooth on), each [i, j]: a visible quad grid on a smooth surface.

quad_edges.description: QuadFace Tools dividing edges (soft, smooth, casting no shadow), each [i, j]: the diagonal of a quad split into two triangles.

tools.name: geometry_create_lines
tools.title: Create Lines
tools.description: Draw many polylines in one call, each as connected edges welded into one curve (selects as one, like a Bezier or freehand line) and painted with its own material: 2D site linework, traced outlines, boundaries, in Adam's edge colours (MTE102 SoftBlack L20, MTE103 DarkGrey L40, MTE104 MidGrey L60). polylines: [{points, closed, material, weld}]; weld defaults to true, closed joins the last point to the first. Lines never fill faces. Wrapped in a new group by default, so they never split or merge with other geometry (wrap_in none puts them straight into the parent, where they can split its coplanar faces). Polylines that meet end to end share their vertices. Materials must exist (material_manage) or be "#RRGGBB". Always pass name. Up to 20,000 polylines and 400,000 points per call.

tools.name: geometry_drape
tools.title: Drape Edges
tools.description: Drape (project) edges straight down onto a surface, like Sandbox Drape but nothing is imprinted: the draped lines are new edges in their own group, so they never stick to the surface. ids: the edges to drape, or groups/components whose edges are used at every depth (2D linework drawn at any height: its z is ignored). surface_ids: the groups/components (or faces) forming the surface. Only faces facing up are used, and where several overlap in plan the highest wins, so a terrain solid's top is used, not its bottom. Each source edge is split wherever it crosses a surface edge in plan, so every piece lies exactly on one face; lift raises them (e.g. 5) if lines flicker over the faces. Each source curve (arc, Bezier, welded polyline) or chain of loose edges becomes one welded curve and keeps its material (edge colour) unless material is given. Parts off the surface are left out and reported. Re-drape after editing the 2D lines: delete the old draped group first.

ids.description: Edges to drape, or groups/components holding them (all their edges, at every depth).

surface_ids.description: Groups/components (or faces) forming the surface to drape onto.

lift.description: Height above the surface for the draped lines (default 0).

tools.name: geometry_extrude
tools.title: Push/Pull or Follow Me
tools.description: Extrude existing faces. mode pushpull: face_ids pushed by distance along each face's front normal (negative = the other way; copy:true keeps the original face, like Ctrl). Distances are world distances even inside scaled groups. mode followme: sweep profile_face_id along a path - either path_edge_ids (edges in the same context as the face) or path_points (world points; drawn in the face's context and removed afterwards unless keep_path). Typical uses: mouldings, cornices, gutters, handrails, pipes, pierced openings.

copy.description: pushpull: leave the starting face in place.

path_points.description: followme: path as points (instead of edges).

keep_path.description: followme with path_points: keep the drawn path edges.

tools.name: geometry_edit
tools.title: Edit Geometry
tools.description: Clean up or modify faces and edges. operation: soften_edges (soft+smooth where faces meet under angle, default 20 degrees), harden_edges, hide_edges, show_edges, reverse_faces, find_faces (heal missing faces on edges), erase_stray_edges (edges with no face), merge_coplanar_faces (remove edges between coplanar faces with the same materials), intersect (Intersect Faces: the groups in ids with each other, or mode with_context with everything around them; new edges go inside each group). ids may be faces, edges or groups/components (then everything inside, recursively unless recursive:false). Editing inside a component changes every copy; make_unique:true isolates the targeted instances first.

make_unique.description: Give shared components their own definition first.

tools.name: solid_boolean
tools.title: Solid Boolean
tools.description: Solid Tools (SketchUp Pro/Studio). target_id is the solid you keep; tool_ids are the other solids, applied in turn. union / intersect / outer_shell merge them; subtract cuts the tools out of the target (result = target minus tools; tools are consumed unless keep_tools); trim cuts the target by the tools and keeps the tools; split returns up to three solids (overlap, target minus tool, tool minus target). All operands must be manifold groups/components in the same parent. The result is a NEW group that inherits the target's name, tag, material, shadow settings and attributes (new id: use the returned id). If the result would be empty or the target would vanish, nothing changes and you get an error instead. Pass every tool in one call (tool_ids) rather than one call per tool. Checked before SketchUp runs: a non-solid operand is described (open edges, internal faces), an inside-out one is refused, and tools that do not reach the target are skipped. SketchUp's engine is slow on dense curved meshes (thousands of faces can take 30 s or more) and can fail or leave holes there: let cutters pass 1 mm beyond the faces they cut and keep segment counts modest.

keep_tools.description: Keep a copy of the tool solids (default false).

result_name.description: Outliner name for the result (default: the target's name; an unnamed target gives e.g. "Cut solid 4000 x 215 x 2400").

tools.name: annotation_create
tools.title: Create Annotation
tools.description: Add annotation. kind: text (leader text at point; leader_vector = offset to the label, leader:false hides the leader), text_3d (3D letters as geometry in their own group: text, height, extrusion, font, bold, italic, filled, align; placed with position / rotation_z / x_axis / z_axis like geometry_create_solid), dimension_linear (start, end, offset_vector = where the dimension line sits), dimension_radial (arc_edge_id = an edge of a circle/arc, leader_point), guide_line (start and end, or start and direction; stipple), guide_point (point). Positions are world by default. Pass name for text_3d so the user can find it in the Outliner.

leader_vector.description: text: offset from point to the label (default 300 mm each axis).

leader.description: text: show the leader line (default true).

offset_vector.description: dimension_linear: offset of the dimension line (default 500 mm in -Y).

direction.description: guide_line through start in this direction (infinite).

tools.name: image_place
tools.title: Place Image
tools.description: Place an image file (png, jpg, bmp, tif, gif, psd, tga) in the model at real size, e.g. a site plan, elevation drawing or reference photo to model over. width in the call's units (height follows the image's proportions unless given). Lies flat on XY at position by default; normal (and x_axis) stand it up, e.g. normal [0,-1,0] faces the front. as_textured_face:true explodes it into a face carrying the image as a texture.

path.description: Absolute path to the image file.

tools.name: section_plane
tools.title: Section Plane
tools.description: Section planes. create: point + normal (the side the normal points to is cut away, e.g. normal [0,0,1] at floor height + 1200 mm gives a plan cut), name, symbol (3 chars), activate (default true). activate: id. deactivate: id or parent_id (switches the cut off in that context). update: id with name/symbol/flip. List existing ones with entity_query types ['SectionPlane']; control their display with view_set section_display.

name.description: Outliner name, e.g. "Section A-A" (default: SketchUp's own "Section 1", "Section 2"...).

tools.name: group_create
tools.title: Make Group
tools.description: Group existing entities (or make them a component with as_component). The entities must all be in the ACTIVE context (open their parent with context_set first if they are inside a group). Optional name, definition_name, description, tag, material for the new group/component. Returns its id and placement. Always pass name: it is how the user finds it in the Outliner.

tools.name: component_place
tools.title: Place Component
tools.description: Place instances of a component: by definition name, definition_id, or skp_path (loads a .skp file as a component definition, e.g. from a component library). position (or positions for many copies at once), rotation_z in degrees, optional x_axis / z_axis, and scale [sx, sy, sz] in the component's own axes (negative mirrors). Placed at world coordinates in any parent at any depth. Returns the new instance ids.

skp_path.description: Absolute path of a .skp to load as a component.

tools.name: component_manage
tools.title: Manage Components
tools.description: Component and group housekeeping. action: make_unique (ids get their own definitions), replace_definition (swap component instances in ids to to_definition / to_definition_id), explode (ids; returns the released entity ids), rename_definition (definition + new_name), set_definition_properties (definition + description and/or behavior: glue_to none/any/horizontal/vertical/sloped, cuts_opening, always_face_camera, shadows_face_sun, is2d, no_scale_mask), save_definition_as (definition + .skp path; overwrite), reset_scale (ids keep position and rotation but lose scaling).

tools.name: entity_transform
tools.title: Transform
tools.description: Move, rotate, scale or mirror entities in world space, optionally as copies or arrays. operations run in order, each {type, ...}: translate {vector}; move_to {position, anchor: origin (single group/component, default then) | bounds_min (default otherwise) | bounds_center | bounds_bottom_center}; rotate {angle degrees, axis (default [0,0,1]), center (default: bounds centre)}; scale {factors [sx,sy,sz] or a number, center}; mirror {normal, center}. Works for groups, components, images and loose geometry at any nesting depth. copies:N makes N copies each moved one step further (a linear or polar array: translate for rows, rotate for rings); copy:true makes one copy. Returns ids and the new world bounds. Do not include an entity together with a group that contains it.

tools.name: entity_delete
tools.title: Delete
tools.description: Erase entities (faces, edges, groups, components, text, dimensions, guides, section planes, images) by id. One undo step (model_undo brings them back). Materials, tags, scenes and definitions are removed with their own tools. Open groups must be closed first.

tools.name: entity_set_properties
tools.title: Set Properties
tools.description: Set Entity Info properties on many entities at once: name (groups/components), tag (created if missing; "Untagged" clears it), hidden, locked (groups/components), casts_shadows, receives_shadows, soft / smooth (edges). Entities that do not have a property are skipped and reported. To paint use material_apply.

tools.name: entity_reparent
tools.title: Move Into Group
tools.description: Move groups and components into another group or component (parent_id; 0 = model root), or into a new group (new_group {name, tag}: made at the root unless parent_id says where), keeping each exactly where it is in the world, with its name, tag, material, hidden, locked, shadow flags and instance attributes. SketchUp cannot move entities between contexts, so each is placed again from its own definition and the original erased: moved objects get new ids, returned in order as ids (a group keeps its geometry and its definition's data). Refused: loose geometry (group it first with group_create), anything open for editing, an id inside another id, a source inside a component used more than once, a destination inside what moves, a shared destination component. Use it to nest elements into storey containers. Tag first, then move: tags travel with the object.

parent_id.description: Destination: 0 = model root, else a group or component id. With new_group: where the new group is made (default root).

new_group.description: Make a new group and move the ids into it, e.g. {"name": "Ground Floor", "tag": "90__Storey__GroundFloor"}.

tools.name: truevision_structure
tools.title: TrueVision Structure
tools.description: Read the model the way the TrueVision GLB Builder exports it, and say what TrueVision will never see. Reports the storey containers (root groups/components on the 90-93 storey tags) with their element groups by tag (walls 21/11, floors 22/12, roofs 23/13, windows 24/14, doors 25/15, stairs 26/16, fixtures 27/17, furniture 28/18, decor 29/19, landscape 07-09, entourage 60-61), the flat files from other root objects, and the GLB file names it will write. Lists every object it skips, with the reason: untagged, helper or excluded tags, a tag that is not an element tag inside a storey, or loose faces and edges directly in a storey. Also lists category tags nested inside exported elements (they export with the element). The rules come from the GLB Builder itself when it is loaded, else from the Tags SSOT file. include_objects lists every object for classifying (name, definition, library code, ADR/AWN assembly, tag, storey, world bounds, faces); analyse_faces adds each object's face area by orientation (up, down, vertical, sloped) and the model's floor levels (the heights with the most upward face area). save_path writes it all to a JSON file. Read-only.

include_objects.description: List every object (paged with limit/offset): root objects, storey children, and objects inside plain container groups.

analyse_faces.description: Add face area by orientation per object and the model's floor levels (slower on big models).

expand_depth.description: Levels listed inside plain container groups (default 2).

max_names.description: Names listed per group in the report (default 8).

save_path.description: Absolute .json path: write the whole report with every object, for scripts.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing save_path file (default false).

tools.name: truevision_export
tools.title: TrueVision Export
tools.description: Read Adam's TrueVision GLB Builder, the plugin that exports a model to TrueVision: everything its dialog shows, nothing changed. action: status (start here: version, model, project link and target scheme, file counts, point cloud and Scene Sync switches, the running job), manifest (every GLB file an export writes, by storey, with its on/off toggle; filter narrows it), project (the link, the portal, every scheme folder with its GLB count and date, the phases with their next folder name, the site plan stores; include_structure adds the project's folder tree), site_plan (the layers on the 71-75 site plan tags with line and face counts, unused tags, checks, and the store it would write into), scenes (Scene Sync: every SketchUp scene, on or off, its type and how it stands against the project), point_clouds (the Point Cloud tab: viewer, scenes, selection, store; check_python adds the Pillow WebP check), job (the last job started through these tools: running, its status line, and its report once it ends; poll about every 10 s, never in a tight loop), fetch_r2 (starts a job that lists the project's GLBs in Cloudflare R2; changes nothing there), r2_inventory (that listing against the scheme folders here: only in R2, not pushed yet, or a different count; folder lists one folder's files), logs (the cloud sync logs and the last export; file shows a log's tail), python (the Python the pipeline uses, and whether Pillow writes WebP), config (the export rules, folder names, design phases and pipeline names the GLB Builder works to). Needs the GLB Builder 2.14.0 or newer.

filter.description: manifest: only files or storeys whose name contains this text.

include_structure.description: project: add the project's TrueVision folder tree.

check_python.description: point_clouds: also check that Python's Pillow writes WebP.

folder.description: r2_inventory: a cloud folder name; lists its files.

file.description: logs: a file name from cloud_logs, or "last_export"; shows its tail.

tail_lines.description: logs: lines of the file's tail (default 80).

limit.description: logs: how many cloud logs to list, newest first (default 10).

tools.name: truevision_export_edit
tools.title: TrueVision Export Edit
tools.description: Change the TrueVision GLB Builder's exports and settings on this model and this computer; nothing reaches Cloudflare R2 (truevision_publish does). action: export_folder (the GLBs into path, any absolute folder), export_project (into the linked project's target scheme folder: the previous export is zipped into 00__Archive first, or cleared with existing: "replace" and confirm; then the switched-on scenes are written, and with Export Point Clouds on the point clouds render as a job), select_files (files from manifest, or all: true; on), link_project (project_code, e.g. "RB05"; the target becomes its latest scheme), unlink_project, dismiss_link_prompt, set_portal_root (path; "" clears), set_target (folder: a scheme folder), create_scheme (phase_id: the phase's next scheme folder, which becomes the target), duplicate_scheme (folder, copied into the next number, which becomes the target), delete_scheme (folder and confirm; moved into 00__Archive, or for good with permanent: true), set_site_plan_store (folder: SitePlan__DrawingData__Existing or __Proposed), create_site_plan_store (variant), export_site_plan (the 71-75 site plan layers into the chosen store, or path; older site plan files are kept unless stale: "delete" with confirm), switch_scenes (scenes: names or ids, on), set_scene_type (scene, type), detach_scene (scene: TrueVision keeps its last sync for good), write_scenes (the Scene Sync manifest into the project), switch_point_clouds (on), select_point_cloud_scenes (scene_ids, on), set_point_cloud_scene (scene_id, values), order_point_cloud_scenes (scene_ids, top to bottom), reload_point_cloud, export_point_clouds (render the selected point cloud scenes into the project, as a job), open_dialog, reload (Reload Scripts, no message box). Exports refuse while a group is open; whatever writes into the project refuses while a job runs. confirm is the linked project's code: pass it only when the user asked for that deletion. Each model setting is one undo step, 'TrueVision: ...'. Not allowed in batch_execute.

path.description: export_folder, export_site_plan: an absolute folder. set_portal_root: the na-project-portal folder, or "" to clear.

existing.description: export_project: the previous export is zipped into 00__Archive (default), or cleared (needs confirm).

material_mode.description: export_folder, export_project: materials in the GLBs (default no_materials, the whitecard).

downscale_textures.description: export_folder, export_project: shrink textures over 1024 px.

files.description: select_files: file names from truevision_export manifest.

project_code.description: link_project: two letters and two digits, e.g. "RB05".

folder.description: set_target, duplicate_scheme, delete_scheme: a scheme folder name. set_site_plan_store: a site plan store name.

phase_id.description: create_scheme: a phase_id from truevision_export project (phases).

permanent.description: delete_scheme: delete for good instead of moving into 00__Archive.

confirm.description: The linked project's code, for delete_scheme, existing: "replace" and stale: "delete" (an unlinked export_site_plan takes the folder's name). Only when the user asked for it.

stale.description: export_site_plan: older site plan GLBs this export did not write (default keep; delete needs confirm).

scenes.description: switch_scenes: scene names or persistent ids.

scene.description: set_scene_type, detach_scene: a scene name or persistent id.

type.description: set_scene_type: what the scene is in TrueVision (auto: from its camera).

scene_ids.description: select_point_cloud_scenes, order_point_cloud_scenes: point cloud scene ids.

scene_id.description: set_point_cloud_scene: a point cloud scene id.

values.description: set_point_cloud_scene: any of viewType, scale (the 1:N denominator), imageWidthPx (500-30000), pointSizePx (null for Auto).

tools.name: truevision_publish
tools.title: TrueVision Publish
tools.description: Publish a TrueVision project to the live site through the TrueVision GLB Builder. Each action runs as a job and answers at once; follow it with truevision_export {action: "job"}. action: push_dry_run (runs the ProjectVision build, which regenerates the master index and EVERY project's data files in the website repo on this computer and drops keys it does not know, then lists what a push would upload and delete in Cloudflare R2; uploads nothing), push (the build, then the R2 sync of the project's TrueVision content: it uploads what changed AND deletes GLBs that are no longer here), export_and_push (export_project, then push), write_scenes_and_push (write_scenes, then push), export_point_clouds_and_push (render the point clouds, then push), purge_r2_folder (delete one scheme folder's GLBs from R2 for good: cloud_folder from a fresh fetch_r2 inventory; refused if R2 changed since), open_pipeline (open the build pipeline console for this project, which syncs it to R2 when run there). Every action but push_dry_run needs confirm set to the linked project's code: pass it only when the user asked for exactly this push or purge in this conversation. Refuses while another job runs. Not allowed in batch_execute.

confirm.description: The linked project's code, e.g. "RB05": every action but push_dry_run. Only when the user asked for it.

cloud_folder.description: purge_r2_folder: a cloud folder from truevision_export r2_inventory.

existing.description: export_and_push: the previous export is zipped into 00__Archive (default), or cleared.

material_mode.description: export_and_push: materials in the GLBs (default no_materials).

tools.name: attributes_get
tools.title: Get Attributes
tools.description: Read attribute dictionaries (custom data stored in the .skp) from entities, component definitions (by their id) and/or the model (model:true). Filter by dictionary and key. Dynamic Components keep their parameters in the 'dynamic_attributes' dictionary; IFC classification data also lives in dictionaries.

tools.name: attributes_set
tools.title: Set Attributes
tools.description: Write attribute values into a dictionary on entities, definitions (by id) and/or the model (model:true). values = {key: value}; a null value deletes that key; delete_dictionary:true removes the whole dictionary. Values may be strings, numbers, booleans or arrays of those (objects are refused: JSON-encode them).

tools.name: material_manage
tools.title: Manage Material
tools.description: Create or update (upsert, default), delete or rename a material. color "#RRGGBB" or a SketchUp colour name; alpha 0-1 (1 = opaque); texture_path with texture_width / texture_height in the call's units (width alone keeps the image's proportions). SketchUp 2025+ PBR: metallic and roughness factors 0-1, normal_texture_path + normal_scale, ao_texture_path + ao_strength, metallic_texture_path, roughness_texture_path. Deleting a material returns anything painted with it to default. Painting is material_apply.

tools.name: material_apply
tools.title: Paint
tools.description: Paint entities with a material (name, "#RRGGBB" plain colour created on demand, or "none" to clear). mode entity (default): the entities themselves - faces take side front/back/both, groups/components pass their material to any default-painted faces inside. mode faces_inside: paint every face inside the given groups/components, recursively (like a deep paint bucket); shared components change in every copy unless make_unique:true.

tools.name: tag_manage
tools.title: Manage Tags
tools.description: Tags (layers). action: create (name or names; optional visible, color, line_style, folder), create_standard (name or names from Adam's Tags SSOT, made by his TagUtils with the SSOT line style, colour and metadata; a name not in the SSOT is refused; existing tags are left as they are unless update_existing), update (name + new_name / visible / color / line_style / folder, "" folder = top level), delete (name or names; contents move to Untagged unless delete_contents:true), set_active, isolate (show only these tags), show_all, create_folder / delete_folder (folder path like "Site/Existing"; deleting keeps its tags). Untagged cannot be renamed, deleted or hidden. To tag entities use entity_set_properties tag.

update_existing.description: create_standard: re-apply the SSOT style to tags already in the model (TagUtils also turns them visible).

tools.name: scene_manage
tools.title: Manage Scenes
tools.description: Scenes (pages). action: create (captures the current view; pass camera / standard_view / zoom / zoom_ids to set the view first; name, description, index, uses, activate), update (re-capture a scene from the current view, optionally after setting the camera), delete, activate (instant, no transition), rename (new_name), reorder (index; 2025+), set_properties (description, transition_time, delay_time, include_in_animation, uses). uses = what the scene remembers: {camera, rendering_options, shadow_info, hidden_geometry, hidden_objects, hidden_layers, section_planes, axes, environment} (omitted = everything).

tools.name: view_get
tools.title: Get View
tools.description: Current view state: camera (eye, target, up, direction, perspective and fov, or parallel height), viewport size in pixels, active scene, style, shadow summary. include rendering_options / shadow_info for every key and value (the keys view_set accepts), sections for the active section planes.

tools.name: view_set
tools.title: Set View
tools.description: Change the view. Camera: camera {eye, target, up, perspective, fov, ortho_height}, standard_view (top, front, iso...; aimed at zoom_ids or the whole model), zoom extents/selection, zoom_ids. Look: face_style (wireframe, hidden_line, shaded, shaded_with_textures, monochrome; applied just after this call), xray, show_hidden_geometry, section_display {planes, cuts}, rendering_options {Key: value} for any key view_get lists. Sun: shadows {on, time "2026-06-21T14:00:00", light, dark, use_sun_for_shading, on_ground, on_faces, or raw ShadowInfo keys}. style (name), style_file (.style path to add and select), update_style (save changes into the style), environment (2025+). Rendering, shadow and style changes are one undo step.

shadows.description: on, time, light, dark, use_sun_for_shading, on_ground, on_faces, or raw ShadowInfo keys.

tools.name: view_capture
tools.title: Capture View
tools.description: See the model: renders the view to an image and returns it to you. Use it to check your work after modelling, and before describing a model. Default 1280 x 800 PNG (smaller costs fewer tokens). Optional camera / standard_view / zoom / zoom_ids aim the shot and the user's view is restored afterwards (restore_view:false leaves it); scene activates that scene first (it stays active). save_path also saves the file (overwrite to replace). transparent background (png), line_scale for thicker lines in large images. include_point_cloud: true also draws Adam's point clouds on show over the image, each with its own look and clip box, exactly where they sit on screen (Na Point Cloud Viewer 0.14.1; the result's point_cloud says what was drawn), so you can check your model against the scan.

include_point_cloud.description: Also draw the point clouds on show over the image (Na Point Cloud Viewer 0.14.1+; from 0.14.5 a scene's cloud look is applied first, and captures over 12 MP keep no clouds, with a warning).

tools.name: model_undo
tools.title: Undo / Redo
tools.description: Undo or redo the last steps (Edit > Undo / Redo). Every model-changing call of this server is exactly one step named "MCP: ...", so steps:1 undoes your last call. Careful: if the user has worked in between, their steps are undone too.

tools.name: sketchup_send_action
tools.title: Send Action
tools.description: Trigger a native SketchUp command by its documented action name, e.g. select a tool for the user (selectPushPullTool:, selectMoveTool:), toggle axes or hidden geometry display. Runs asynchronously just after this call returns, and Sketchup.send_action is deprecated from SketchUp 2026.2: prefer the dedicated tools (view_set, model_undo, camera...). Only the names in the enum (from SketchUp's documentation) are accepted.

tools.name: ruby_eval
tools.title: Ruby
tools.description: Run Ruby inside SketchUp for anything the other tools do not cover (bulk queries, custom geometry, calling the user's own Na__ plugins). Ready locals: model, entities (active), selection, view. The last expression's value is returned (plus 'value' when it is plain JSON data), with anything printed. Runs as one undo step and is rolled back entirely on any error (transaction:false to skip). Before writing code, verify every API method with ruby_api_lookup: the code is linted against the official API index and unknown methods are returned as warnings. SketchUp lengths are inches internally (use 2400.mm, x.to_mm); angles are radians (90.degrees). Coordinates inside an open group are world coordinates. Modal dialogs are auto-answered; code cannot be interrupted, so avoid long loops. Refused when the user switched eval off or enabled read-only mode.

transaction.description: Wrap in one undo step, rolled back on error (default true).

tools.name: asset_library
tools.title: Asset Library
tools.description: Adam's component library, used the way the Component Editor Tools Gallery and Index use it (needs Na Noble3d Modelling Tools). The library root is the Gallery's library folder; its top folders are sets (default Na__CoreLib__3dAssets). Convention: NN__Category/NN_S000__Series/NN_NNNN__Series__Item__Descriptor__Type-01__Size__.skp, NN mirrors the SSOT tag numbers, and the component inside is named exactly like the file. action: overview (sets, category and series folders, counts, next free code per series, tag and taxonomy maps, recent journals), browse (files with code, folder and cached gallery data; filter folder, category, series, kind, query; paged), get (one file: definition name, size in mm, description, Na__ComponentLibrary data and a naming check; include_thumbnail returns the Gallery thumbnail), next_code (the next free NN_NNNN in a series or family, with neighbours and the name template), check_name (a name against the convention, codes already taken included), audit (stragglers, duplicate codes, prefix and folder mismatches, bad names, suggested fixes; deep opens files to compare the name inside). Read-only: files are opened in an operation that is always rolled back, so the open model never changes.

set.description: Library set: a top folder of the library (default Na__CoreLib__3dAssets) or its Gallery alias.

category.description: Category number or folder, e.g. "13" or "13__Building__Roof".

query.description: browse: text in the file name, gallery name, definition name, category or type.

path.description: get: the .skp, absolute or relative to the library root.

name.description: check_name: a file or definition name.

deep.description: get (default true): open the file for the definition name, size and library data. audit: open up to deep_limit files to compare the name inside with the file name.

include_thumbnail.description: get: return the Gallery thumbnail image.

include_blocked.description: Include blocked folders such as 00__Archive and 00__Retired.

count.description: next_code: how many free codes to list.

tools.name: asset_library_edit
tools.title: Asset Library Edit
tools.description: Change Adam's component library through the Component Editor Tools rules (needs Na Noble3d Modelling Tools). action: save (a component from the open model, by definition, definition_id or instance_id, into folder / series / category; code defaults to the next free one; name = the segments after the code; library_data gallery_name, category, type, notes; the file's component is named like the file and a blank category / type is filled from the folder; rename_in_model also renames it in the model as one undo step), rename (path to code, name, new_name and/or new_folder: file and component renamed together), move (path to new_folder), update (library_data, description, def_name), archive (zip a file into its set's 00__Archive as <name>__30-Sep-2026.zip, checked before the original leaves), create_folder (NN__Category or NN_S000__Series), apply_plan (many steps checked together first; dry_run defaults to true; then applied in order within time_budget_s), revert (a journal), refresh (make an open Gallery re-scan). Every change is journaled under <library>/00__Archive/00__McpLibraryJournals with byte copies of rewritten files, so revert restores the originals; nothing is deleted. Refuses existing targets, codes used twice, names that break the convention (force accepts them) and files placed in the open model (allow_in_use). Not allowed in batch_execute. Agree names and codes with the user before saving or renaming.

set.description: Library set: a top folder of the library (default Na__CoreLib__3dAssets) or its Gallery alias.

folder.description: save: the folder inside the set it goes in. create_folder: the folder to make.

category.description: Category number or folder, e.g. "13" or "13__Building__Roof".

path.description: rename / move / update / archive: the file, absolute or relative to the library root.

definition.description: save: the component definition's name in the open model.

instance_id.description: save: a placed instance whose component is saved.

code.description: NN_NNNN. save: omit to take the next free code in the series or family.

name.description: save / rename: the segments after the code, e.g. "Roof__RidgeFinial__FleurDeLis__Type-02" (the code and trailing __ are added).

new_name.description: rename: the whole new name (instead of code / name).

new_folder.description: rename / move: the destination folder inside the set.

def_name.description: The component inside the file: "auto" (default) = named like the file, "keep" = leave it, or a name.

library_data.description: Na__ComponentLibrary fields: gallery_name, category, type, notes, truevision_valid ("true"/"false"), code (override) and custom keys.

fill_taxonomy.description: save (default true): fill a blank category / type from the folder.

rename_in_model.description: save: also rename the component in the open model to its library name (one undo step).

overwrite.description: save: replace an existing file (the old one is kept in the journal).

allow_in_use.description: Edit a file whose component is placed in the open model (the placed copy is what gets written).

force.description: Accept names that break the convention.

plan.description: apply_plan: {title, steps: [{op, from, to, path, library_data, def_name, why}]}; op is create_folder, rename_folder, move_file, archive_file, rename_asset or update_asset. Paths relative to the library root are safest.

plan_file.description: apply_plan: a JSON plan file instead of plan.

journal.description: revert: the journal to undo. apply_plan: continue a paused or failed journal.

dry_run.description: apply_plan defaults to true (check only, change nothing); the other actions default to false.

time_budget_s.description: apply_plan: stop between steps after this long (default 45).

tools.name: entity_studio
tools.title: Entity Studio
tools.description: Read Adam's Element Assembly Studio Pro (Entity Studio Pro): his parametric windows, exterior doors, interior doors and cabinets (2.6.0 or newer). type is one of casement, sash, single, double, bifold, sliding, interior_door, base, drawers, wall, tall, wardrobe. action: status (version, types, setting counts, presets, dialog open); parameters (type: every setting the dialog shows, from its own control files: with no filter the sections and their keys; query / section / keys give label, unit, min, max, step, options, start value, section and what it needs. Values outside these are refused, never clamped); elements (every placed element at any depth: instance_id, id such as AWN001 / ADR002 / ACB001, type, size_mm, world origin, along axis, bounds, copies; type / query filter); inspect (instance_id: identity, size, metadata, the stored values that differ from a new one (all: true for every one; keys / prefix narrow), parts, MOD groups and fielded panels with solid and volume); openings (wall_id: every opening in a wall group, left to right seen from outside, with width, height, depth, sill and head z and the points A, B, D the opening tools would pick; outside or outside_point says which side is outside, default away from the model's middle; path when the wall's component is used more than once); list_presets (family, type, query; archived: true lists the archive); get_preset (code; keys / prefix); assets (kind: handles, architraves, hinges, cabinet_handles, cabinet_legs, sash_horns, window_boards, finishes, edge_colours: the keys the dropdowns and finish cards offer); list_handles. Lengths mm. Read-only.

query.description: parameters: words in a key, label, section or condition. elements: part of an id or name. list_presets: text in the code, name, description or keywords.

section.description: parameters: one section of the tab, e.g. size, lights, opening, leaves, glazing, panels, frame, sashes, hardware, finish, output.

keys.description: parameters / get_preset / inspect: only these setting keys (door and cabinet keys may drop their Na__DoorConfig__ / Na__CabinetConfig__ prefix).

prefix.description: get_preset / inspect: only keys starting with this, e.g. "single_door_".

all.description: inspect: every stored value, not only those changed from a new element.

family.description: list_presets: Window, ExteriorDoor, InteriorDoor or Cabinet.

archived.description: list_presets: the presets in the archive instead.

kind.description: assets: one kind (all when left out).

wall_id.description: openings: the wall: a group or component whose own faces are the wall.

path.description: openings: instance path to the wall, only when its component is placed more than once.

outside.description: openings: a direction pointing out of the building through the wall, e.g. [0, -1, 0].

outside_point.description: openings: any point on the outside of the wall.

tools.name: entity_studio_edit
tools.title: Entity Studio Edit
tools.description: Create, change and maintain Element Assembly Studio Pro windows, exterior doors (single, double, bifold, sliding), interior doors and cabinets through the dialog's own build pipelines: each build or rebuild is ONE undo step with the plugin's own name (e.g. 'Create Window', 'Update Bifold Door'). action: build (type and/or preset, values on top; placed into opening {wall_id, index} (from entity_studio openings) or {point_a, point_b, point_d}: fit (default true) sizes it as Measure Opening would, height less the cill; or at position + direction (along the wall, left to right seen from outside); cabinets take run {point_a, point_b, side (a point on the room side)} and run_offset mm; name gives the name tail; dry_run checks everything and builds nothing); update (instance_id: values merged onto its stored ones, or preset (keep_size default true), reset (keys back to a new element's), opening refits the size only; never moves it; every copy of the definition changes; returns the changed values; dry_run); rename (instance_id, name: the tail after the coded head); export_dxf (file: absolute .dxf; from instance_id, preset or type; windows and single / double doors; overwrite); save_preset (name agreed with Adam first; from instance_id, preset or type plus values), update_preset (code: name / description / keywords and/or values or instance_id; keeps a .bak), archive_preset / restore_preset (code: moved to and from the archive, never deleted), refresh_preview (code; dialog open), open_dialog (instance_id selects it so the dialog shows it), reload. values use the dialog's keys (entity_studio parameters lists them with ranges): out-of-range values, unknown keys and options the dialog does not offer are refused. Builds go at the model root. Not allowed in batch_execute.

type.description: build / save_preset / export_dxf: what to make (from its starting values).

preset.description: build / update / save_preset / export_dxf: start from this preset's values, e.g. "EAS008".

values.description: Setting keys and values on top (mm, true/false, an option's value). entity_studio parameters lists them.

tools.name: point_cloud_state
tools.title: Point Cloud State
tools.description: Read the model's point clouds in Adam's Na Point Cloud Viewer (needs it loaded, 0.13.1 or newer). The viewer draws clouds as an overlay: view_capture shows them only with include_point_cloud, and no point can be picked or snapped to, so measure with point_cloud_slice, point_cloud_fit and point_cloud_heightmap. Per cloud: id (pc_xxxxxxxx), name, colour, shown, loaded, points, file, source_unit, look (point_size_px, opacity_percent, colour_mode), bounds, clip (enabled, min, max, size), clip_scene (the one showing, and whether its box was changed since) and clip_scenes (id, name, box), every length in the call's units; cache (path and exists: the viewer's .napc point cache, for the skill's offline numpy kit) and local_to_model (12 numbers in model INCHES, R*k row-major then t; null when not loaded). Also overlay_on, point_budget and active_cloud. clouds narrows it to some clouds (ids or names). Read-only.

tools.title: Point Cloud Clip
tools.description: Set or switch a point cloud's clip box through Adam's Na Point Cloud Viewer. A clip box is axis-aligned in model coordinates, one per cloud, saved in the cloud's record in the model: each change is ONE undo step of the viewer's own, named "Point Cloud: ...", so model_undo steps 1 reverts it. Clip only when the user asked to work the cloud, and put their clip scene back when done (action scene). action: box (min, max), around (ids: their world bounds grown by margin, default the viewer's selection margin of 100 mm, rounded outwards onto its 5 mm grid, as Clip Box Around Selection does), on and off (clipping on or off, the box kept), scene (cloud, and scene: a clip scene id or name from point_cloud_state, or "full" for the whole cloud). box and around also show those clouds and switch the overlay on. clouds: ids or names; default every cloud on show (the active cloud when none is), as Draw Clip Box does. label names the undo step (default "MCP Clip Box"). Not allowed in batch_execute.

The viewer remembers each cloud's look on this computer, as its sliders do. clouds: ids or names (default every cloud). shown (each cloud's Show switch), point_size_px (1 to 10), opacity_percent (5 to 100), colour_mode (rgb; black, best over the model; primary, each cloud in its own colour), point_budget (points drawn per frame, shared by every cloud on show, 10,000 to 50,000,000), overlay (SketchUp's overlay switch, every cloud), reload: true starts the viewer's own Reload of every cloud that is not loaded (it loads in the background: check point_cloud_state). Values outside the viewer's limits are refused. Note what you change and set it back if the user's view should stay as it was.

tools.name: point_cloud_slice
tools.title: Point Cloud Slice
tools.description: Measure a point cloud inside a box at the speed of the viewer's native engine, without Python (points and density need Point Cloud Viewer 0.14.0). Every action takes min and max (the box, model axes, the call's units) and cloud (id or name; default the only loaded cloud on show). action: count (every point in the box, exact); histogram (axis x, y or z and bin: points per bin along that axis, one pass over the cloud whatever the bins, up to 10,000; peaks (local maxima holding at least peak_share, default 0.2, of the highest bin; 'at' is their weighted centre, finer than a bin) and percentiles p1 to p99. Levels from z (treads, floors, rail tops), faces from x or y (walls, risers, post faces), repeats along a run (spindle rhythm)); points (limit points, default 1,000: an even sample of the points in the box, as the viewer stores clouds shuffled; up to 1,500 come back in the reply in the call's units, and with save_path up to 5,000,000 go to a .npz (p: model mm, c: colour) that numpy and the skill's pc_kit.py read); image (view and resolution per pixel: the viewer's renderer draws the box looking along a model axis, black points on white, the nearest point winning each pixel: shape); density (the same frame, darker = more points behind each pixel, log scale unless scale linear, with max_per_pixel and p99_5_per_pixel: planes and edges stand out, as pc_kit.py render). image and density take grid (a line every grid length, every fifth darker) and overlay_ids (the model's edges in red over the slice, overlay_clip to keep only what is inside the box; viewer 0.14.1), and return the PNG with u and v: the model value at its left and top edges and per pixel. right looks along -X with +Y to the right, left along +X, front along +Y, back along -Y, top down with +X right. save_path keeps the PNG, or the points' .npz. frame (viewer 0.14.6) turns the box, the view and every position to any angle: along a wall not square to the model, up a roof. The cloud must be loaded (point_cloud_state). Read-only.

tools.name: point_cloud_fit
tools.title: Point Cloud Fit
tools.description: Fit a shape to the points of a point cloud inside a box, so you read its numbers instead of guessing them from a histogram (Na Point Cloud Viewer 0.14.2; the rules below from 0.14.5). shape: plane (normal, pointing up, or for a wall within about 1 degree of plumb its larger horizontal part positive; a point, offset, slope_deg from level, azimuth_deg of the normal: the way the plane falls, or the way a wall faces; its extent; orientation horizontal for a floor or tread, when offset is the level, vertical for a wall, riser or post face, or any); line (direction uphill, so start is the low end, end, length, slope_deg above level, azimuth_deg the way it rises: a rail, an edge, a kerb); circle (seen along axis x, y or z: centre, radius, the arc the points cover: a bullnose step or a round post in plan, a pipe in section; max_radius, default the box's larger side, stops a straight piece passing for a huge circle; when the points settle on two different circles, a curve that is not one arc, a warning gives both); cylinder (a circle along axis plus from, to and length); box (seen along axis: width, depth, rotation_deg, centre, from, to, corners, with trim percent, default 1, taken off each side, its rms and p95 each point's distance from the sides: a post, a newel, a pier). The fit is robust (RANSAC on an even sample of the box, then least squares on the points within tolerance, default 10 mm, until they stop changing), extents run the full length (the 1st to 99th percentiles widened by what they trim), and every answer reports rms, p95 and inlier_share, with warnings when few points fit. For a small round thing set tolerance to the scan's noise (2 to 3 mm). Results are only as good as the box: look first with point_cloud_slice density, box one thing tightly, and where an arc runs into a straight piece at a tangent end the box where the curve ends. Read-only.

tools.name: point_cloud_check
tools.title: Point Cloud Check
tools.description: Check a built model against the point cloud: how far the scan sits from every face shown in the groups, components or faces in ids (Na Point Cloud Viewer 0.14.3; hidden groups, faces and tags inside them are left out from MCP 1.0.17). An even sample of the cloud in the box round them (their world bounds grown by margin, default 100 mm, or min and max) is measured to the nearest face within reach (default 50 mm); farther points belong to other things and count as away. Returns overall rms, mean, p50, p95, max and within_share (the share within tolerance, default 10 mm); the same for each part (each group or component shown directly inside an id, the worst first); the worst spots (where points beyond tolerance gather); and warnings when few points reach the model or it sits offset as a whole. Sign: positive means the scan lies outside the faces (the model is too small there), negative inside (the model is proud). With view (top, front, back, left, right) and resolution, a heatmap of the sample: green within tolerance, red outside, blue inside, pale grey away, with the model's edges; grid and point_size_px as for point_cloud_slice; save_path keeps it. sample: points measured (default 20,000, up to 100,000). Read-only.

tools.name: point_cloud_heightmap
tools.title: Point Cloud Heightmap
tools.description: Heights from the point cloud, per cell of a grid or along a path (Na Point Cloud Viewer 0.14.4). An even sample of the points (sample, default 1,000,000, about 2 s; up to 5,000,000) gives each cell or station the stats asked for: min, max, mean, median or p<percent> (default p2, p50, p98). A percentile is the value at rank floor(q x (n - 1)), so p2 finds the ground under grass and p98 the tops of walls, kerbs and rails. view (default top: z for each x, y cell; front, back, left or right: how far a wall stands out along y or x; in every view a cell's values are ranked by nearness to the viewer, so max and p98 are the surface seen). action grid (default): the box min, max in cells resolution wide (default 50 mm). Returns each statistic's range, the best plane's slope (percent, 1 in N, the way it falls and, from the top, its azimuth: degrees anticlockwise from +x), the cell mapping, the values of show (default p50) inline up to 2,500 cells, and a picture: show from blue (low) to red (high), shaded, contours every contour (default picked; 0 none), white where empty, overlay_ids' edges in magenta (overlay_clip as for point_cloud_slice). save_path: a .npz in pc_terrain.py's rasters.npz layout (x0, y1, res, W, H, count, z02, z50, z98 ..., model mm, NaN where empty; colours adds rgb_top and rgb_low), or from the top an .asc ESRI grid of show. action profile: path (2 to 50 points; from the top z is ignored), a corridor width wide (default 100 mm), stations step long (default 50 mm). Returns show's start, end and rise, its least-squares slope, the steepest metre, a table of stations (chainage, position, count, stats) up to 1,000, and a picture: chainage across, height up (exaggeration picked to show falls, or given), the corridor's points grey, each statistic a line. min and max, if given, trim the corridor (e.g. under a tree). save_path: .csv or .npz. frame (viewer 0.14.6) turns the box, view and path to any angle (a roof slope, a wall off the model axes). image_path keeps the picture. Read-only.

tools.name: agent_outliner
tools.title: Agent Outliner
tools.description: What Adam has left for agents in his Agent Outliner (Na Noble3d Modelling Tools): the flags and comment threads on objects, the standard names he gives them, and what was made or changed, by him or by an agent. Start a job with summary. action: summary (what waits for you, what changed since you last acknowledged, flag counts), inbox (every object Adam flagged For Agent, Question or Check This, or commented on, that no agent has acknowledged: its id, path, tag, size, what its standard name means, its flag and whole thread; and the model's own thread when he wrote there), changes (made, changed or erased since your last acknowledge, or since_seq / since; by: user shows Adam's own edits, the silent corrections to learn from; each says who and which fields: name, tag, material, transform, definition, contents), thread (whole threads by ids, or model: true), threads (every thread on one line: open or resolved, waiting_on agent (answer it) or user (Adam has not answered yours yet), the last word; status and waiting_on narrow it), flags (every flagged object by flag type with each type's meaning, Do Not Touch and Reference included: never change those; flag and by narrow it), prefixes (the standard names such as CAD__FrontElevation, what each means, and which objects carry it: how to find the CAD elevations and references he points you to), find (the Outliner's search: words, tag:, type:, is:new, by:agent, flag:for_agent, -term, a | b), tags (every tag: colour, shown, folder, object count; move objects with agent_outliner_edit tag), tag_tree (Adam's Tree by Tag view, how he groups the model: tag folders, then tags, then each tag's objects as trees; an untagged part sits inside its tagged group; tag: one card, depth: levels), category_tree (his Group by Category view, the same by naming category and prefix; prefix: one card). Entries may carry images (pictures pasted in the Chat tab), each with its path on this PC: open it to see what he means. Read-only. Answer with agent_outliner_edit.

tools.name: agent_outliner_edit
tools.title: Agent Outliner Edit
tools.description: Write to Adam through his Agent Outliner (needs Na Noble3d Modelling Tools); he reads it in the Outliner beside each object. action: reply (answer a thread Adam started, by ids or model: true; marks what you answered as read), comment (start or add to a thread: a question, what you did and why; model: true for a summary of your work), resolve / reopen (close or reopen a thread, text optional), flag (flag objects for Adam: check_this, question, reference, do_not_touch, done; text adds a note), unflag, acknowledge (mark Adam's comments and flags as read: ids, model: true, or everything waiting when neither is given; changes: true also marks every recorded change as seen, so the next changes call starts after it; this PC only, no undo step), name (give objects a standard name: prefix = a label or id such as CAD__FrontElevation or REF, in the mode Adam set; names only, never tags), strip (take a standard prefix off again: REF__Wall becomes Wall; a name that was exactly a label is left empty, with a warning), tag (put the objects on one tag: tag = a name from agent_outliner tags, "Untagged" or "" for none; a missing tag is refused with the model's tags named unless create: true, which makes it in the same step: ask Adam before making tags). images (comment / reply): picture files on this PC to show Adam, e.g. a view_capture saved with save_path (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, 15 MB each, 8 at most); they are copied into his ChatFromAgents folder and shown in the Chat tab; text may then be left out. While his messages wait, every tool result carries an outliner notice; reply or acknowledge and it stops. author signs your entries, e.g. 'Claude (bay window session)': sign every entry, as his Chat tab lists each agent by it. Each change to the model is one undo step 'MCP: Agent Outliner Edit'. Keep comments short and factual.
