side.description: Which side of the cut moves (default above).

stretch.description: Lengthen without distorting the mouldings: e.g. [{axis: 'z', at: 50, by: 30}] makes it 30 taller above z 50.

flip.description: Mirror left to right about the datum.

datum.description: [y, z]: this point becomes 0,0, the point that rides on the path.

local_name.description: The name a local profile carries (default the profile's own).

reverse.description: create / recreate: the profile on the other side of the path.

rotation_step.description: Quarter turns of the profile about the path.

origin_offset.description: [y, z] mm: the profile point that rides on the path; [0, 0] clears it.

start_offset.description: mm the sweep runs past (+) or short of (-) the start of an open run, as given.

end_offset.description: mm past (+) or short of (-) its end.

parent_id.description: create / recreate: the group or component the trace (or its wrapper) goes in; omit for the active context, 0 for the model root.

origin.description: World origin of the wrapper (default the path's lowest corner).

reference_path.description: Draw the path as loose edges in the wrapper (default true).

wrapper.description: create: Adam's pattern, a named group holding the reference path and the trace.

reference_path.description: create without a wrapper: also draw the path as loose edges beside the trace.

reference_path_material.description: create: an edge material already in the model for the reference path edges (e.g. MTE102__LineColour__SoftBlack__L20); unpainted when omitted.

name.description: create / recreate / rename: the trace's name (default the plugin's Na__ProfileTrace__<key>).

tag.description: create: an existing tag for the wrapper, else the trace.

tools.name: profile_tracer_library
tools.title: Profile Tracer Library
tools.description: Adam's profile library files (the Gallery's presets, 04__Data__ProfileLibrary) through the Profile Path Tracer's own writers. Never the model, not undoable, not allowed in batch_execute. Only on Adam's say-so for that profile: he decides case by case what is added or changed; otherwise keep a reshaped profile local to its trace. action: save_new (a new profile: name required, code optional; geometry from from_trace (a trace's local profile), profile_key + profile_edit, profile_outline, profile_json or profile_face_id; short_name, description, keywords), overwrite (new geometry for profile_key from any of those, or profile_edit alone to reshape it in place; confirm = the key; the old file kept as .bak), set_meta (name, short_name, description, keywords), rename_file (file_name), redatum (datum [y, z] becomes 0,0; .bak), flip (left to right; .bak), delete (confirm = the key; the file is set aside beside itself as .deleted__<time> unless permanent: true). Profile lengths are mm.

profile_key.description: A library profile key (profile_tracer profiles lists them).

confirm.description: overwrite / delete: the profile key again, only when Adam asked for exactly this.

code.description: save_new: the key and file name (default from the name).

from_trace.description: save_new / overwrite: a trace (persistent id or NPT id) whose profile to save.

profile_outline.description: A new outline: points [[y, z], ...] in mm (y across, z up, 0,0 rides on the path; one closed loop, no closing repeat), arcs [{start, segments, radius}] as runs of the loop, edge_colour an SSOT edge colour id for every edge.

edge_colours.description: One colour id (or null) per edge.

vertex_colours.description: One colour id (or null) per vertex: the line it sweeps along the path.

profile_edit.description: profile_edit: reshape the profile; the result goes on the trace as its own local profile (the library file is untouched). Applied in this order.

size.description: Scale the axis named to this size in mm.

keep_aspect.description: size: scale both axes by the one given.

at.description: mm: the cut line in the profile's own coordinates.

by.description: mm the points beyond the cut move (negative moves them the other way).

side.description: Which side of the cut moves (default above).

stretch.description: Lengthen without distorting the mouldings: e.g. [{axis: 'z', at: 50, by: 30}] makes it 30 taller above z 50.

flip.description: Mirror left to right about the datum.

datum.description: [y, z]: this point becomes 0,0, the point that rides on the path.

base_profile_key.description: save_new from an outline: the profile whose edge colour it takes.

datum.description: redatum: [y, z] mm, the point that becomes 0,0.

permanent.description: delete: delete the file outright instead of setting it aside.

tools.name: ruby_api_lookup
tools.title: SketchUp API Lookup
tools.description: Look up the official SketchUp Ruby API (2,087 methods, 156 classes and modules, up to SketchUp 2026.1, from SketchUp's own ruby-api-stubs) so you never guess a method. query: a class ('Sketchup::Face'), a method ('Face#pushpull', 'Sketchup.send_action', 'pushpull'), or words ('section plane', 'exporter options') -> signatures, version added, summary, parameters, return value, example, docs link. code: Ruby to check -> every method name it calls that exists neither in the SketchUp API nor in Ruby core, with suggestions. live:true also asks the running SketchUp whether each method exists there.

tools.name: batch_execute
tools.title: Batch
tools.description: Run several tool calls in ONE round trip and ONE undo step. steps: [{"tool": "geometry_create_solid", "arguments": {...}}, ...]. A string argument "$<step>.<path>" is replaced by a value from an earlier step's result, e.g. "$0.id" or "$2.ids.0", so you can create something and then move, paint or tag it in the same batch. atomic (default true): if any step fails, every step is undone and you get each step's outcome. atomic:false keeps the steps that worked (stop_on_error decides whether to continue). rollback:true is a zero-trace trial: every step runs and you get each result (captures saved to disk stay), then every step is undone, nothing changes, and the activity log reads 'Trial' instead of FAILED; camera moves and scene changes are not undone. model_file and nested batches are not allowed; context_set only when atomic is false. Ideal for building assemblies (walls, stairs, arrays of components) quickly.

rollback.description: Trial: run every step, return the results, then undo them all (default false). Needs atomic.

tools.name: sketch_read
tools.title: Read Sketch
tools.description: Read what Adam sketched to show intent: rough lines, arcs and freehand he drew and selected, plus the notes and dimensions he wrote beside them. The fastest way to get a shape from him: ask him to draw it roughly in SketchUp and select it. Edges (also inside selected groups, any depth) are chained into polylines (ends within snap join), each split into straight runs and fitted arcs (within tolerance) and returned in world coordinates: runs (line or arc with centre, radius, sweep and how far his line strays from it) and clean_path (lines as their two ends, arcs resampled to Adam's segment budget), ready to pass to geometry_offset_band as path_points. Notes come back with the numbers in them in the call's units ('1100', '1.1m', '150 wall') and the polyline they sit beside; dimensions with their lengths. Default: the current selection; ids reads those instead. A sketch is intent, not a survey: say the rule back in numbers and get Adam's yes before building. Read-only.

ids.description: Read these (edges, faces, groups, texts, dimensions) instead of the selection.

snap.description: Line ends closer than this join (default 5 mm).

tolerance.description: How far a run may stray from its fitted line or arc (default 15 mm).

tools.name: input_pick
tools.title: Pick Points
tools.description: Ask Adam to click points in SketchUp and get them back exactly, snapped by SketchUp's own inference (endpoints, edges, faces, axes). Use it instead of guessing a position from a photo or a screenshot: 'click where the lawn edge meets the terrace', 'trace the bed edge'. action: start (prompt says what to click; mode points, polyline or polygon; max_points; round_to snaps the answer to a grid, e.g. 5), then tell Adam in chat what to click and call wait (polls until he presses Enter or double-clicks, presses Esc, or wait_s runs out; returns early when he writes in the Agent Outliner), or result to look without waiting, or cancel. He clicks to add a point, Backspace removes the last, Enter or a double-click finishes, Esc cancels; the picked line is drawn in red as he goes. Points come back in world coordinates in the call's units. Changes nothing in the model; it does change the active tool, so it is not allowed in a batch.

prompt.description: start: what Adam should click, shown in SketchUp's status bar.

max_points.description: start: finish by itself after this many points.

round_to.description: start: round the picked coordinates to this step (e.g. 5 for the 5 mm grid).

pick_id.description: result / wait / cancel: the id start returned (default the latest).

wait_s.description: wait: how long to wait for Adam (default 180 s).

tools.name: proposal_preview
tools.title: Proposal Preview
tools.description: The gate before building anything that is not fixed by CAD, a drawing, an orthophoto, a scan or the model: draw the proposal as red 2D lines (a group PROPOSAL__<name> at the model root), capture it from above, and ask Adam. action: draw (lines: [{points, closed}], labels: [{text, point}] for the numbers, e.g. '150 wall', '970 bed'; ask: the question, posted with the picture beside the proposal in his Agent Outliner; author signs it; capture false skips the picture), wait (polls his Agent Outliner thread until he answers, up to wait_s; he may answer in chat instead), status (his replies so far), clear (name, or all: true, when the real thing is built or he says no), list. Redrawing a name replaces it. Build nothing from a site photo until he has said yes. Drawing and clearing are one undo step each; the question is the Agent Outliner's own step. Not allowed in a batch.

name.description: The proposal's name, as Adam would call it (PROPOSAL__ is added).

z.description: Draw every point at this height (e.g. just above the paving) so existing solids never hide the lines.

note.description: draw: kept on the proposal (what rule it shows).

ask.description: draw: the question for Adam, posted in the Agent Outliner with the picture.

capture.description: draw: take the top-view picture (default true).

wait_s.description: wait: how long to wait (default 300 s).

tools.name: geometry_offset_band
tools.title: Offset Bands
tools.description: Turn a rule into geometry in one call: bands at parallel offsets from a path. The way to build planters, raised beds, retaining walls, kerbs, paths, edgings and lawn lines that follow a terrace or wall edge, once Adam has given the numbers. Path: path_points (world points, e.g. a sketch_read clean_path) or path_ids (one connected line of edges). Offsets are true parallels: positive to the LEFT of the path's direction (side: right flips), straight runs mitred, drawn arcs offset radially so bands stay concentric. Each band is a named group inside one wrapper group (name, tag): a solid from z0 to z1 between offsets from and to (hollow: wall thickness makes a ring wall round an open band; end_inset [start, end] pulls its ends in), or line_only at one offset (at) and z, for a lawn edge. Ends: square to the path, or start_line / end_line (two world points each) such as the paving's straight edge. Faces under soften_angle (default 15) are softened; edge_material paints the edges. Every solid must close or nothing is built. Example (Corrett planter): bands [{name wall, from 0, to 1270, z1 200, hollow 150}, {name bed, from 150, to 1120, z1 120, end_inset [150, 150]}, {name lawn line, line_only, at 2300}]. One undo step.

path_points.description: The path in world coordinates (its z is ignored: bands carry their own).

path_ids.description: Or: edges, a curve, or a group of edges forming one connected line.

closed.description: The path is a loop (rings, no end lines).

side.description: Which side positive offsets go, walking the path (default left).

arc_tolerance.description: Vertices fitting an arc within this are offset radially (default 1 mm).

start_line.description: Two world points: the line the bands start on.

end_line.description: Two world points: the line the bands end on.

hollow.description: Wall thickness: the band becomes a ring wall.

tools.name: model_snapshot
tools.title: Model Snapshot
tools.description: Record objects as they are now, to compare later or in another window with model_diff: per object its name, tag, world bounds, solid and volume, counts, edge and face material tallies, its plan footprint (every face looking straight up, by level) and the same for its direct children (child_depth). Always mm and litres. save_path writes it as JSON (take one of your work before Adam reviews it, then diff his corrected version against it). Read-only; the file is the only thing written.

include_data.description: Return the whole snapshot in the result (large).

tools.name: model_diff
tools.title: Model Diff
tools.description: Measure two versions of the same thing against each other: what you built against Adam's redraw, before and after he tidied it, this window against a snapshot from another. a and b are each {id} (an object in this window) or {snapshot: path, object: name or id} (a model_snapshot file). Reports plan overlap (IoU, area only in a, only in b), how far apart the outlines are (max, medians, the worst spot), bounds moved, volume, solid, counts, and which edge and face materials changed; children are paired by name, then by best overlap, and compared the same way. Use it whenever Adam has redrawn or repainted your work: record what he changed as lessons. Always mm and litres. Read-only.

tools.name: image_rectify
tools.title: Rectify Site Photo
tools.description: Lay a site photo (drone, phone) flat on the ground in the model, or on any plane, rectified by a homography fitted to four or more pairs of photo pixel and model point, so you and Adam can see where things in it sit against the model. FOR CONTEXT ONLY: a site photo is a reference, never a spec; anything off the plane (walls, plants, people) is smeared, and nothing in it is measured for building. Ask Adam for the numbers, or CAD, an orthophoto or a scan, before modelling from it. pairs: [{pixel: [u, v] from the photo's top left, world: [x, y, z] ON the plane}], spread round the area (paving corners, wall bases). z sets the ground plane (default 0); plane {origin, x_axis, y_axis} for any other. region (two opposite world corners) or margin limits the area; the part beyond the horizon is left off. Placed as REF__SitePhoto__<name> at the model root (opacity default 0.75). Reports the fit in pixels and in ground distance, and checks SketchUp's mapping against it. One undo step.

path.description: Absolute path to the photo (PNG or JPEG).

region.description: Two opposite world corners of the area to cover.

margin.description: Without region: how far past the control points to cover (default 25 % of their spread).

tools.name: image_flatten
tools.title: Flatten Photo onto a Rectangle
tools.description: Flatten part of a photo onto a rectangle on its plane, as SketchUp's free-pin Position Texture then Make Unique Texture would, to draw over like a CAD sheet. For something flat and rectangular whose width you know (a window or door opening from the CAD, a panel, a facade). corners are the four texture pins in the photo (pixels as viewers show it, EXIF rotation applied); rectangle is where they go in the model. Without rectangle.height, points fix it (known positions with their pixels, fitted by least squares, e.g. glazing bar crossings from the CAD); with neither, it is estimated from the photo's perspective (rough). The photo is warped into a new square-on PNG (never written over; by default in the job's 01__ReferenceFiles/11__Photos__Flattened) mapped plainly onto a face over the rectangle plus margin: REF__PhotoPlane__<name> (opacity 0.75), with the rectangle's outline in its own group. Reports the fit at every pin and point in pixels and on the plane, the height and where it came from, and the output's pixel size. Only what lies on the plane is true to scale (reveals, cills and pipes are shifted). One undo step.

path.description: Absolute path to the photo (PNG or JPEG; convert WebP first).

corners.description: The rectangle's four corners in the photo, pixels [u, v] from its top left as photo viewers show it (a JPEG's EXIF rotation is undone for you), in this order: the origin corner, the corner along x_axis, the far corner, the corner along y_axis.

origin.description: World position of the origin corner.

x_axis.description: Along the width, in the plane.

y_axis.description: Across it, in the plane, towards the far side.

height.description: The side along y_axis, when known.

at.description: Along x_axis and along y_axis from the origin corner.

points.description: Known positions with their pixels (at, or world): they tighten the fit and, without height, fix it.

margin.description: How much of the photo to keep round the rectangle, every side (default 0).

pixel_size.description: Output pixel size (default: the photo's finest detail on the plane).

max_pixels.description: Cap on output pixels (default 4,000,000; about 1.4 s a megapixel).

save_path.description: Absolute .png path for the flattened image (refused if it exists).

outline.description: Draw the rectangle's outline in its own group (default true).
